review.verdict: The palette and bubble/chart/label props are on-model, but the intended split-panel layout collapsed into a cream-top/blue-horizon scene, the chart overlaps the teen's torso, and the figure stands outside a bed with an unreadable phone prop — these composition and polish bugs pull the average below the pass bar.
revisionNotes: Rebuild the split background per the scene spec: a true left/right paper vs. ink division, not a cream top / blue horizon — the current layout loses the panel contrast the brief relies on.
Fix the anchor collision between chart1 and teen: the bar chart overlaps the figure's torso; attach it to chatbubble's right side with a bigger offset so it stays in the left panel.
Render teen in the specified 'sit' pose, in bed, with glow1 visibly lighting the face — currently the figure stands with no bed, and the glow circle floats disconnected beside it.
Right-third is crowded (chart1, teen, bubble2, label1, glow1 all compressed together) while the left panel is sparse; rebalance scale/spacing so neither side reads cluttered or empty.
Clean up the teen's leg/foot, which clips into the blue ground shape — tighten that silhouette so it doesn't look cut off.
Make the held phone prop clearer (increase its scale/contrast) so 'still keeps chatting' reads without needing the caption.

review.verdict: The riso-duotone style is consistent, but the key metaphor breaks down: the safety label floats disconnected from its bubble, the teen appears to be standing on a bench rather than lying in bed, and the button/chart read as scattered props rather than a bubble 'sprouting' controls — the joke doesn't land without re-reading the brief.
revisionNotes: Reattach label1 (the red safety tag) directly to bubble2's corner — it currently floats isolated near the top-right, so the 'peeling label' metaphor is lost.
Rebuild 'bed': the teen reads as standing/balancing atop a bench, not sitting in bed. Give it a headboard/pillow silhouette and change teen's pose to a seated recline.
Visually connect chart1 and button1 to chatbubble (overlap or a short connector) so they read as 'sprouting' from the bubble instead of three unrelated floating shapes.
Fix glow1: it merges into the teen's head as a pink blob. Drop offset so it sits behind the phone/torso as a light pool, not touching the head outline.
Tighten composition: left panel has scattered elements with dead space between them; right panel is crowded at top and empty below. Group each panel around one clear focal cluster.
Add a visible phone-glow cue on the teen's face or hands so 'late-night crisis chat' is legible without relying on the text label alone.

review.verdict: Good concept and correct casting (human teen, AI bubble), but the right-hand panel has rendering bugs — the bed shape double-exposes through the teen's torso, the phone is missing despite being central to the metaphor, and the legs/label look disconnected — pulling clarity and polish down enough to fail.
revisionNotes: Fix the "bed" raw shape: it currently double-exposes behind the teen's torso, making the figure look merged with a screen/monitor rather than sitting on a bed — redraw as a simple headboard+mattress silhouette that sits clearly behind, not through, the body.

Render the phone: the teen's props say holds="phone" but no phone shape is visible in the hands; add a small rectangle phone with the glow circle wrapped directly around it so the late-night light source actually reads.
The chest glow circle currently reads as a stray dark smudge on the torso instead of a warm phone glow — recolor it lighter/warmer and anchor it tight to the phone, not floating mid-chest.
The bottom blanket bar crops the legs into a disconnected dark mark; raise the blanket offset or redraw the legs so they read as clearly tucked underneath.
The red safety-label tag floats loosely near the teen's shoulder with no clear attachment — tighten its offset so it visibly peels off bubble2's corner, matching the brief's metaphor.
Button1's ring is clipped by the chatbubble's rounded corner in a way that looks accidental; nudge its offset right by ~15px so the full circle reads as intentionally attached.
